page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-32xCPU-384GB is a memory-optimized virtual server based on the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 shared vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 12.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate a balanced profile with notable multi-threaded capabilities. While single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by stress-ng single-core and gzip compression results, multi-threaded operations perform well. Specifically, bzip3 multi-threaded decompression ranks in the top 25% of tested systems. Other multi-core metrics, including Geekbench multi-core, PassMark CPU, and software compilation tests, consistently fall within the average range.

Memory bandwidth and database operations also demonstrate stable, average performance. The system achieves average speeds in both small-block cached and large-block uncached memory reads, as well as large-block uncached memory writes. Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput align with these average benchmarks. This hardware profile offers high resource density, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads requiring large memory footprints without the premium of dedicated CPU cores.

Given the high memory capacity and average multi-threaded performance, this server is suited for memory-intensive workloads such as database operations, caching layers, and multi-threaded data processing. However, it is less suitable for tasks that depend heavily on single-core CPU speed or local high-speed storage.
